h:
Package strings implements simple functions to manipulate UTF-8 encoded strings.

For information about UTF-8 strings in Go, see https://blog.golang.org/strings.

Builder.h: A Builder is used to efficiently build a string using Builder.Write methods. It minimizes memory copying. The zero value is ready to use. Do not copy a non-zero Builder.

Builder.Cap.h: Cap returns the capacity of the builder's underlying byte slice. It is the total space allocated for the string being built and includes any bytes already written.

Builder.Grow.h: Grow grows b's capacity, if necessary, to guarantee space for another n bytes. After Grow(n), at least n bytes can be written to b without another allocation. If n is negative, Grow panics.

Builder.Len.h: Len returns the number of accumulated bytes; b.Len() == len(b.String()).

Builder.Reset.h: Reset resets the Builder to be empty.

Builder.Write.h: Write appends the contents of p to b's buffer. Write always returns len(p), nil.

Builder.WriteByte.h: WriteByte appends the byte c to b's buffer. The returned error is always nil.

Builder.WriteRune.h: WriteRune appends the UTF-8 encoding of Unicode code point r to b's buffer. It returns the length of r and a nil error.

Builder.WriteString.h: WriteString appends the contents of s to b's buffer. It returns the length of s and a nil error.

Clone.h: Clone returns a fresh copy of s. It guarantees to make a copy of s into a new allocation, which can be important when retaining only a small substring of a much larger string. Using Clone can help such programs use less memory. Of course, since using Clone makes a copy, overuse of Clone can make programs use more memory. Clone should typically be used only rarely, and only when profiling indicates that it is needed. For strings of length zero the string "" will be returned and no allocation is made.

Compare.s: func strings.Compare(a string, b string) int
Compare.h:
Compare returns an integer comparing two strings lexicographically. The result will be 0 if a == b, -1 if a < b, and +1 if a > b.

Use Compare when you need to perform a three-way comparison (with slices.SortFunc, for example). It is usually clearer and always faster to use the built-in string comparison operators ==, <, >, and so on.

Contains.s: func strings.Contains(s string, substr string) bool
Contains.h: Contains reports whether substr is within s.

ContainsAny.s: func strings.ContainsAny(s string, chars string) bool
ContainsAny.h: ContainsAny reports whether any Unicode code points in chars are within s.

ContainsFunc.s: func strings.ContainsFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) bool
ContainsFunc.h: ContainsFunc reports whether any Unicode code points r within s satisfy f(r).

ContainsRune.s: func strings.ContainsRune(s string, r rune) bool
ContainsRune.h: ContainsRune reports whether the Unicode code point r is within s.

Count.s: func strings.Count(s string, substr string) int
Count.h: Count counts the number of non-overlapping instances of substr in s. If substr is an empty string, Count returns 1 + the number of Unicode code points in s.

Cut.s: func strings.Cut(s string, sep string) (before string, after string, found bool)
Cut.h: Cut slices s around the first instance of sep, returning the text before and after sep. The found result reports whether sep appears in s. If sep does not appear in s, cut returns s, "", false.

CutPrefix.s: func strings.CutPrefix(s string, prefix string) (after string, found bool)
CutPrefix.h: CutPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string and reports whether it found the prefix. If s doesn't start with prefix, CutPrefix returns s, false. If prefix is the empty string, CutPrefix returns s, true.

CutSuffix.s: func strings.CutSuffix(s string, suffix string) (before string, found bool)
CutSuffix.h: CutSuffix returns s without the provided ending suffix string and reports whether it found the suffix. If s doesn't end with suffix, CutSuffix returns s, false. If suffix is the empty string, CutSuffix returns s, true.

EqualFold.s: func strings.EqualFold(s string, t string) bool
EqualFold.h: EqualFold reports whether s and t, interpreted as UTF-8 strings, are equal under simple Unicode case-folding, which is a more general form of case-insensitivity.

Fields.h: Fields splits the string s around each instance of one or more consecutive white space characters, as defined by unicode.IsSpace, returning a slice of substrings of s or an empty slice if s contains only white space.

FieldsFunc.s: func strings.FieldsFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) []string
FieldsFunc.h:
FieldsFunc splits the string s at each run of Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) and returns an array of slices of s. If all code points in s satisfy f(c) or the string is empty, an empty slice is returned.

FieldsFunc makes no guarantees about the order in which it calls f(c) and assumes that f always returns the same value for a given c.

FieldsFuncSeq.s: func strings.FieldsFuncSeq(s string, f func(rune) bool) iter.Seq[string]
FieldsFuncSeq.h: FieldsFuncSeq returns an iterator over substrings of s split around runs of Unicode code points satisfying f(c). The iterator yields the same strings that would be returned by FieldsFunc(s), but without constructing the slice.

FieldsSeq.h: FieldsSeq returns an iterator over substrings of s split around runs of whitespace characters, as defined by unicode.IsSpace. The iterator yields the same strings that would be returned by Fields(s), but without constructing the slice.

HasPrefix.s: func strings.HasPrefix(s string, prefix string) bool
HasPrefix.h: HasPrefix reports whether the string s begins with prefix.

HasSuffix.s: func strings.HasSuffix(s string, suffix string) bool
HasSuffix.h: HasSuffix reports whether the string s ends with suffix.

Index.s: func strings.Index(s string, substr string) int
Index.h: Index returns the index of the first instance of substr in s, or -1 if substr is not present in s.

IndexAny.s: func strings.IndexAny(s string, chars string) int
IndexAny.h: IndexAny returns the index of the first instance of any Unicode code point from chars in s, or -1 if no Unicode code point from chars is present in s.

IndexByte.s: func strings.IndexByte(s string, c byte) int
IndexByte.h: IndexByte returns the index of the first instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

IndexFunc.s: func strings.IndexFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) int
IndexFunc.h: IndexFunc returns the index into s of the first Unicode code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

IndexRune.s: func strings.IndexRune(s string, r rune) int
IndexRune.h: IndexRune returns the index of the first instance of the Unicode code point r, or -1 if rune is not present in s. If r is utf8.RuneError, it returns the first instance of any invalid UTF-8 byte sequence.

Join.h: Join concatenates the elements of its first argument to create a single string. The separator string sep is placed between elements in the resulting string.

LastIndex.s: func strings.LastIndex(s string, substr string) int
LastIndex.h: LastIndex returns the index of the last instance of substr in s, or -1 if substr is not present in s.

LastIndexAny.s: func strings.LastIndexAny(s string, chars string) int
LastIndexAny.h: LastIndexAny returns the index of the last instance of any Unicode code point from chars in s, or -1 if no Unicode code point from chars is present in s.

LastIndexByte.s: func strings.LastIndexByte(s string, c byte) int
LastIndexByte.h: LastIndexByte returns the index of the last instance of c in s, or -1 if c is not present in s.

LastIndexFunc.s: func strings.LastIndexFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) int
LastIndexFunc.h: LastIndexFunc returns the index into s of the last Unicode code point satisfying f(c), or -1 if none do.

Lines.h: Lines returns an iterator over the newline-terminated lines in the string s. The lines yielded by the iterator include their terminating newlines. If s is empty, the iterator yields no lines at all. If s does not end in a newline, the final yielded line will not end in a newline. It returns a single-use iterator.

Map.s: func strings.Map(mapping func(rune) rune, s string) string
Map.h: Map returns a copy of the string s with all its characters modified according to the mapping function. If mapping returns a negative value, the character is dropped from the string with no replacement.

NewReader.h: NewReader returns a new Reader reading from s. It is similar to bytes.NewBufferString but more efficient and non-writable.

NewReplacer.h:
NewReplacer returns a new Replacer from a list of old, new string pairs. Replacements are performed in the order they appear in the target string, without overlapping matches. The old string comparisons are done in argument order.

NewReplacer panics if given an odd number of arguments.

Reader.h: A Reader implements the io.Reader, io.ReaderAt, io.ByteReader, io.ByteScanner, io.RuneReader, io.RuneScanner, io.Seeker, and io.WriterTo interfaces by reading from a string. The zero value for Reader operates like a Reader of an empty string.

Reader.Len.h: Len returns the number of bytes of the unread portion of the string.

Reader.ReadAt.s: func (r *strings.Reader) ReadAt(b []byte, off int64) (n int, err error)

Reader.ReadRune.s: func (r *strings.Reader) ReadRune() (ch rune, size int, err error)

Reader.Reset.h: Reset resets the Reader to be reading from s.

Reader.Seek.s: func (r *strings.Reader) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error)

Reader.Size.h: Size returns the original length of the underlying string. Size is the number of bytes available for reading via Reader.ReadAt. The returned value is always the same and is not affected by calls to any other method.

Reader.WriteTo.s: func (r *strings.Reader) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error)

Repeat.s: func strings.Repeat(s string, count int) string
Repeat.h:
Repeat returns a new string consisting of count copies of the string s.

It panics if count is negative or if the result of (len(s) * count) overflows.

Replace.s: func strings.Replace(s string, old string, new string, n int) string
Replace.h: Replace returns a copy of the string s with the first n non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new. If old is empty, it matches at the beginning of the string and after each UTF-8 sequence, yielding up to k+1 replacements for a k-rune string. If n < 0, there is no limit on the number of replacements.

ReplaceAll.s: func strings.ReplaceAll(s string, old string, new string) string
ReplaceAll.h: ReplaceAll returns a copy of the string s with all non-overlapping instances of old replaced by new. If old is empty, it matches at the beginning of the string and after each UTF-8 sequence, yielding up to k+1 replacements for a k-rune string.

Replacer.h: Replacer replaces a list of strings with replacements. It is safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines.

Replacer.Replace.h: Replace returns a copy of s with all replacements performed.

Replacer.WriteString.s: func (r *strings.Replacer) WriteString(w io.Writer, s string) (n int, err error)
Replacer.WriteString.h: WriteString writes s to w with all replacements performed.

Split.h:
Split slices s into all substrings separated by sep and returns a slice of the substrings between those separators.

If s does not contain sep and sep is not empty, Split returns a slice of length 1 whose only element is s.

If sep is empty, Split splits after each UTF-8 sequence. If both s and sep are empty, Split returns an empty slice.

It is equivalent to SplitN with a count of -1.

To split around the first instance of a separator, see Cut.

SplitAfter.h:
SplitAfter slices s into all substrings after each instance of sep and returns a slice of those substrings.

If s does not contain sep and sep is not empty, SplitAfter returns a slice of length 1 whose only element is s.

If sep is empty, SplitAfter splits after each UTF-8 sequence. If both s and sep are empty, SplitAfter returns an empty slice.

It is equivalent to SplitAfterN with a count of -1.

SplitAfterN.s: func strings.SplitAfterN(s string, sep string, n int) []string
SplitAfterN.h:
SplitAfterN slices s into substrings after each instance of sep and returns a slice of those substrings.

The count determines the number of substrings to return:

  • n > 0: at most n substrings; the last substring will be the unsplit remainder;
  • n == 0: the result is nil (zero substrings);
  • n < 0: all substrings.

Edge cases for s and sep (for example, empty strings) are handled as described in the documentation for SplitAfter.

SplitAfterSeq.s: func strings.SplitAfterSeq(s string, sep string) iter.Seq[string]
SplitAfterSeq.h: SplitAfterSeq returns an iterator over substrings of s split after each instance of sep. The iterator yields the same strings that would be returned by SplitAfter(s, sep), but without constructing the slice. It returns a single-use iterator.

SplitN.s: func strings.SplitN(s string, sep string, n int) []string
SplitN.h:
SplitN slices s into substrings separated by sep and returns a slice of the substrings between those separators.

The count determines the number of substrings to return:

  • n > 0: at most n substrings; the last substring will be the unsplit remainder;
  • n == 0: the result is nil (zero substrings);
  • n < 0: all substrings.

Edge cases for s and sep (for example, empty strings) are handled as described in the documentation for Split.

To split around the first instance of a separator, see Cut.

SplitSeq.s: func strings.SplitSeq(s string, sep string) iter.Seq[string]
SplitSeq.h: SplitSeq returns an iterator over all substrings of s separated by sep. The iterator yields the same strings that would be returned by Split(s, sep), but without constructing the slice. It returns a single-use iterator.

Title.h:
Title returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters that begin words mapped to their Unicode title case.

Deprecated: The rule Title uses for word boundaries does not handle Unicode punctuation properly. Use golang.org/x/text/cases instead.

ToLower.h: ToLower returns s with all Unicode letters mapped to their lower case.

ToLowerSpecial.s: func strings.ToLowerSpecial(c unicode.SpecialCase, s string) string
ToLowerSpecial.h: ToLowerSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their lower case using the case mapping specified by c.

ToTitle.h: ToTitle returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their Unicode title case.

ToTitleSpecial.s: func strings.ToTitleSpecial(c unicode.SpecialCase, s string) string
ToTitleSpecial.h: ToTitleSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their Unicode title case, giving priority to the special casing rules.

ToUpper.h: ToUpper returns s with all Unicode letters mapped to their upper case.

ToUpperSpecial.s: func strings.ToUpperSpecial(c unicode.SpecialCase, s string) string
ToUpperSpecial.h: ToUpperSpecial returns a copy of the string s with all Unicode letters mapped to their upper case using the case mapping specified by c.

ToValidUTF8.s: func strings.ToValidUTF8(s string, replacement string) string
ToValidUTF8.h: ToValidUTF8 returns a copy of the string s with each run of invalid UTF-8 byte sequences replaced by the replacement string, which may be empty.

Trim.s: func strings.Trim(s string, cutset string) string
Trim.h: Trim returns a slice of the string s with all leading and trailing Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

TrimFunc.s: func strings.TrimFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) string
TrimFunc.h: TrimFunc returns a slice of the string s with all leading and trailing Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

TrimLeft.s: func strings.TrimLeft(s string, cutset string) string
TrimLeft.h:
TrimLeft returns a slice of the string s with all leading Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

To remove a prefix, use TrimPrefix instead.

TrimLeftFunc.s: func strings.TrimLeftFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) string
TrimLeftFunc.h: TrimLeftFunc returns a slice of the string s with all leading Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

TrimPrefix.s: func strings.TrimPrefix(s string, prefix string) string
TrimPrefix.h: TrimPrefix returns s without the provided leading prefix string. If s doesn't start with prefix, s is returned unchanged.

TrimRight.s: func strings.TrimRight(s string, cutset string) string
TrimRight.h:
TrimRight returns a slice of the string s, with all trailing Unicode code points contained in cutset removed.

To remove a suffix, use TrimSuffix instead.

TrimRightFunc.s: func strings.TrimRightFunc(s string, f func(rune) bool) string
TrimRightFunc.h: TrimRightFunc returns a slice of the string s with all trailing Unicode code points c satisfying f(c) removed.

TrimSpace.h: TrimSpace returns a slice of the string s, with all leading and trailing white space removed, as defined by Unicode.

TrimSuffix.s: func strings.TrimSuffix(s string, suffix string) string
TrimSuffix.h: TrimSuffix returns s without the provided trailing suffix string. If s doesn't end with suffix, s is returned unchanged.
